evals.prompt: Our giveaway just ended. 1,800 entrants, 6,000 views, 9,000 entries, 400 invalid, ran 14 days with 6 entry methods. We wanted email subscribers. How did we do?
evals.expected_output: Calculates 1,800 / 6,000 = 30% Conversion Rate and 9,000 / 1,800 = 5 Entries per Entrant, places 1,800 in the 1k to 2.5k band below the median, reads 30% conversion against the 37% clean peer figure and the 34% platform average, asks for or reads the per-action counts to judge the email action, gives at most three changes each tied to a figure and to the next piece of work, ends with the next decision.
assertions: Shows 1,800 Entrants / 6,000 views = 30% Conversion Rate and 9,000 Entries / 1,800 Entrants = 5 Entries per Entrant, with the units and denominators clear
States the band and position for contestants

Compares Conversion Rate with the clean peer population for six Actions, identifies any broader comparison population separately, and includes sample sizes and missing-data notes for dataset statistics
Does not benchmark invalid entries
Recommends at most three changes, each naming the next piece of work in the reader's own words
No abstract good or bad verdict

evals.prompt: Conversion was only 19% on our 45-day giveaway with a daily bonus entry. Is something broken?
evals.expected_output: Explains impressions count once per user per day so a 45-day run with a daily action lowers the rate, compares to the 31 to 60 day figure of 24% and the 23% for 61 days or more, says nothing is necessarily broken, and points to what would show a real problem (contestants for the band, the asset action uptake).
assertions: Explains the impressions definition
Compares to the duration row
Does not call the result bad
Names what to check next

evals.prompt: Style check applied to every conversational reply above.
evals.expected_output: Run the prize-picker evals/style_check.py on the saved reply.
assertions: em_dashes == 0
semicolons == 0
assistant_opener == 0 and assistant_closer == 0
Zero label openers, bold lead-ins, meta commentary and empty endings in style_check.py output
No mechanic is banned on the strength of an average, only on a rule, a law or a money risk

evals.prompt: Day 4 of a 14 day giveaway. Impressions were 900 on day 1 and 610 yesterday. 130 Entrants so far, 3,100 Impressions in total. Is this pace normal and is anything wrong?
evals.expected_output: Says the campaign is live, day 4 of 14, and does not rank it. Reads yesterday against day one as a multiple (about two thirds) beside the 14 day row for day 4, names the row, and says a fall from day one is the typical shape. Says the table is Impressions only with no spread, so it cannot say how far under is unusual and gives no Entrant pace. Reads Conversion Rate so far (Entrants over Impressions) against the run length so far, labelled rough. Picks reach, conversion or broken with the figure that decides it.
assertions: States it is live and does not call any figure a result
Compares yesterday over day one with the 14 day row for the day and names the row
Says the curve is Impressions and gives no Entrant pace
Says the table has no spread
Labels the conversion read as rough

evals.prompt: Our giveaway is on day 9 of 21, Impressions are fine but Entrants have been flat since Tuesday at 2am and nobody has entered since. Is it broken, and should I extend?
evals.expected_output: Reads the shape as something broken rather than reach or conversion: Impressions arriving with Entrants stopped at one clock time. Gives the cheap checks (entry link in every place posted, the embed, verification step, email provider sync, any change made at that time, one test entry signed out on a phone) and takes the time of the last Entry from the export. Says extension goes through the terms check and gives no figure for what added days bring in. Never invents a base rate.
assertions: Reads flat Entrants with live Impressions as broken
Lists the cheap checks and a signed-out test entry
Takes the last Entry time from the export
Says nothing in the data measures what added days bring in
Sends any change of date through the terms check
